## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Sources disagree about the wave size this break works in.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best swell direction.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best wind direction.
- Only one independent source confirms the best tide.

| Variable | Research confidence | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Swell direction | Moderate | Supported by 2 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Swell size | Low | Supported by 3 independent sources, including a surf magazine; 1 disagrees. |
| Swell period | Moderate | Supported by 2 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Wind | Moderate | Supported by 3 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Tide | Moderate | Supported by one source (a surf magazine). |
| Bottom / bathymetry | Moderate | Described by 3 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |
| Season | Moderate | Supported by 2 independent sources, including a surf magazine. |
| How the wave breaks | High | Described by 5 independent sources, including a forecast site's spot guide. |

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Read directly: WSL 2015 breakdown, WSL 2018 event guide (one publisher), Surf-Forecast (identity confirmed as the WA Surfers Point), WannaSurf ('Margaret river left' page), Perth is OK! (2019/2023), Surf Europe. Could not read (403): margaretriver.com x2, SurferToday, surfnerd. A WSL page carrying a Surfline event forecast (posts/499542) was read but not used: it is forecast text. SWELL DIRECTION: SW-WSW (WSL table), WSW (Surf-Forecast), inside the optimum. WIND: east (WSL table, Surf-Forecast); WSL's text also says a light SE blows offshore; WannaSurf lists an SE-E-NE window. TIDE: WSL 'Tide: Any' supports the profile's 'all'. PERIOD: mid-long (WSL), groundswell more common (Surf-Forecast); no seconds. SIZE: WSL table 4-15 ft+, WSL guide 2-20 ft, WannaSurf to 16 ft+ (scales not stated). WSL also says the right disappears at about 10 ft and that beyond 12-15 ft 'all bets are off' (closeouts linking with The Box). The profile's 20 ft max rests on the guide's 2-20 ft and the general 'handles about as big as you want'. SEASON: two regional magazine statements (Perth is OK!, Surf Europe) say autumn (Mar-May) is best; Surf-Forecast says all year (not comparable). Nothing supports the profile's Jun and Sep-Oct. BATHYMETRY: a deep-water reef with the shallow Surgeon's Table ledge (WSL); WannaSurf says reef with sharp rocks. No survey or peer-reviewed study was found (Crossref searches returned nothing relevant).

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 2–3 ft | documented | S2, S7 | `wave_height_min_ft` 4 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | 4–15 ft; open top: yes [S1] · double overhead to the 20-foot range [S5] | conflicting | S1, S5 | no separate setting; working range 4–20 ft |
| Maximum suitable | 20 ft [S2, S5] · 16 ft and over (open-ended) [S7] · 12–15 ft; meaning: beyond this all bets are off [S2, S1] | conflicting | S1, S2, S5, S7 | `wave_height_max_ft` 20 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: The 2018 WSL guide says it produces excellent waves from about 2 ft and WannaSurf says it starts working below 1 m / 3 ft; neither states whether these are face or offshore swell heights.
  - S2 (World Surf League): “Main Break is a lefthand and righthand reefbreak that can produce excellent waves anywhere from 2-to-20 feet.”
  - S7 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at Less than 1m / 3ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over”
- **Ideal range**: The 2015 WSL table gives best-conditions swell height as 4-15 ft and more (scale not stated), while SurferToday (search summary, not read directly) says it works better from double overhead to 20 ft.
  - S1 (World Surf League): “Surfers Point (MR) Best Conditions Swell Height: 4-15'+”
  - S5 (SurferToday): “the most important surf break is the Main Break, also known as Surfers Point. This is a powerful left-hander that works better as it goes from double overhead to the 20-foot range.”
- **Maximum suitable**: The 2018 WSL guide says excellent waves up to 20 ft and SurferToday (search summary) says the 20-foot range, but the same WSL guide says all bets are off after 12-15 ft and the 2015 WSL breakdown says the right disappears at 10 ft; WannaSurf's top bracket (16 ft and over) is open-ended; scales are not stated.
  - S2 (World Surf League): “Main Break is a lefthand and righthand reefbreak that can produce excellent waves anywhere from 2-to-20 feet.”
  - S5 (SurferToday): “the most important surf break is the Main Break, also known as Surfers Point. This is a powerful left-hander that works better as it goes from double overhead to the 20-foot range.”
  - S7 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at Less than 1m / 3ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over”
  - S2 (World Surf League): “After Main Break hits 12-to-15 feet, all bets are off.”
  - S1 (World Surf League): “Once Main Break hits 10 feet high, the right begins to disappear”

Notes:

- **Prime months**: Perth is OK! and Surf Europe both name the austral autumn (March-May) as the best season.
  - S8 (Perth is OK!): “Autumn is undoubtedly the best time of year to go surfing in WA – with winter on the horizon intense low pressure systems to the south whip up some serious swells”
  - S9 (Surf Europe magazine): “the austral autumn is a fine season for swell, wind, weather, water temp. You can get waves any time of course, but autumn tends to be when the locals recommend.”
- **Secondary season**: Surf Europe says you can get waves any time but no excerpt names a secondary season.
- **Swell sources**: Perth is OK! says low-pressure systems to the south whip up the autumn swells, and Surf-Forecast says groundswells are more common than windswells.
  - S8 (Perth is OK!): “Autumn is undoubtedly the best time of year to go surfing in WA – with winter on the horizon intense low pressure systems to the south whip up some serious swells”
  - S6 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Groundswells are more common than windswells”
- **Wind patterns**: Surf Europe calls autumn a fine season for wind but no excerpt describes the prevailing or seasonal wind pattern.

  - S1 (World Surf League): “Just watch out for the Surgeon's Table: The shallow ledge occasionally contorts the final section of the wave”
  - S7 (WannaSurf): “TypeReef-rocky...BottomReef (coral, sharp rocks etc..)”

## Conflicting information

- **Swell height · ideal range**: The 2015 WSL table gives best-conditions swell height as 4-15 ft and more (scale not stated), while SurferToday (search summary, not read directly) says it works better from double overhead to 20 ft.
- **Swell height · maximum suitable**: The 2018 WSL guide says excellent waves up to 20 ft and SurferToday (search summary) says the 20-foot range, but the same WSL guide says all bets are off after 12-15 ft and the 2015 WSL breakdown says the right disappears at 10 ft; WannaSurf's top bracket (16 ft and over) is open-ended; scales are not stated.
